Ivan’s Arbor Group Personal Accident wording lists the Simple Fracture benefit limit as S$5,000 per insured person per accident and says a simple fracture confirmed by X-ray is payable at the percentage shown for the bone; its table lists 50% for a leg (tibia or fibula), but the uploaded documents do not establish that the certificate’s S$400,000 sum assured is the current amount in force.

passage.text:
Thigh (femur)                                 60%
Leg (tibia or fibula)                         50%
Arm (humerus, radius or ulna)                 40%
Finger or toe                                 10%
4.2 Other Fracture
Other Fracture: for a compound fracture, or a fracture of a bone not listed in 4.1, we will pay 5% of the Sum Insured shown for the Insured Person under Group Personal Accident in the Certificate of Group Insurance.

passage.text:
Section 6 - Definitions
Accident means a sudden, unforeseen and involuntary event caused by external, violent and visible means.
Simple fracture means a closed fracture where the skin is not broken.
Compound fracture means a fracture where the broken bone pierces the skin.
